title.value: From plane crashes to algorithmic harm: applicability of safety engineering frameworks for responsible ML
title.justification: The title succinctly captures the central theme of the paper, which is the applicability of safety engineering frameworks to managing algorithmic harm in machine learning systems.
title.quote: From plane crashes to algorithmic harm: applicability of safety engineering frameworks for responsible ML

extractions.description: The paper investigates the use of safety engineering frameworks, specifically System Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA) and Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), in managing social and ethical risks associated with machine learning systems. Through interviews with industry practitioners, the study explores current social and ethical risk management practices and discusses how these safety frameworks can be adapted to improve these practices.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is the applicability of safety engineering frameworks for managing social and ethical risks in machine learning systems, rather than focusing on climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Inappropriate design and deployment of machine learning (ML) systems leads to negative downstream social and ethical impact – described here as social and ethical risks – for users, society and the environment.

primary_category.justification: The paper is not directly tied to any specific category of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development as it focuses on the application of safety frameworks to manage social and ethical risks in ML systems.
primary_category.quote: We examine the dialogue between safety engineering frameworks and understandings of social and ethical risks of ML systems.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not address any specific sub-category within the Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development framework, focusing instead on the general applicability of safety frameworks in machine learning ethics.
primary_sub_category.quote: We interviewed 30 industry practitioners on their current social and ethical risk management practices, and collected their first reactions on adapting safety engineering frameworks into their practice.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper explores the integration of safety engineering frameworks into the risk management practices of machine learning systems, addressing social and ethical challenges.
new_primary_category.quote: We propose the use of safety engineering frameworks in machine learning research and practice, and study its impact on responsible ML practices.

new_primary_sub_category.value: Social and Ethical Risk Management in AI
new_primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category focuses on addressing the social and ethical risks associated with machine learning systems through structured safety engineering frameworks.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Our findings suggest STPA/FMEA can provide appropriate structure toward social and ethical risk assessment and mitigation processes.
